title: Canadian cultural output grows while cultural jobs contract, with broadcasting up and film/video down
source_unit: Statistics Canada National Culture Indicators, fourth quarter 2025 and first quarter 2026, Table 36-10-0652-01
geography: Canada; national culture and sport sectors and selected subdomains

observations.period: Fourth quarter 2025 to first quarter 2026; culture and sport production

denominator.unit: Canadian national culture and sport economic-account series; GDP measured in thousands of dollars and jobs measured as jobs

culture_real_gdp_qoq.unit: percent quarter-over-quarter change in real GDP at 2017 constant prices

culture_jobs_qoq.unit: percent quarter-over-quarter change in culture-sector jobs

sport_real_gdp_qoq.unit: percent quarter-over-quarter change in real sport-sector GDP

sport_jobs_qoq.unit: percent quarter-over-quarter change in sport-sector jobs

output_jobs_tension.value: real culture GDP +0.6% while culture-sector jobs -0.3%

mechanism.value: Cultural economic growth does not automatically convert into employment growth; production, pricing, productivity, subdomain mix, and worker bargaining can move differently

observations.method: Descriptive extraction from Statistics Canada Table 36-10-0652-01, using real GDP at 2017 constant prices and jobs for the culture and sport totals; quarter-over-quarter changes were calculated where not directly stated.
observations.uncertainty: These are national economic-account estimates, not worker-level earnings, job quality, hours, contracts, firm survival, or household welfare. GDP and jobs use different accounting concepts and the divergence is not a causal productivity estimate.
observations.subgroup: Canadian culture and sport sectors at the national level.
observations.counterinterpretation: A small job decline can coexist with seasonal adjustment, occupational composition changes, productivity, multiple-job counting, or revisions; GDP growth does not prove improved worker security or cultural supply.

observations.period: Fourth quarter 2025 to first quarter 2026; selected culture subdomains

denominator.unit: Canadian national culture subdomain economic-account series; real GDP at 2017 constant prices and jobs

broadcasting_real_gdp_qoq.unit: percent quarter-over-quarter change in real broadcasting GDP

broadcasting_jobs_qoq.unit: percent quarter-over-quarter change in broadcasting jobs

film_video_real_gdp_qoq.unit: percent quarter-over-quarter change in real film-and-video GDP

film_video_jobs_qoq.unit: percent quarter-over-quarter change in film-and-video jobs

organized_sport_real_gdp_qoq.unit: percent quarter-over-quarter change in real organized-sport GDP

subdomain_mechanism.value: The culture sector is internally heterogeneous: broadcasting GDP rose around major sports-media events while film/video jobs and organized-sport GDP fell, so 'the cultural economy' is not one consumer or labor market

observations.method: Descriptive extraction and quarter-over-quarter calculation from Statistics Canada Table 36-10-0652-01 for broadcasting, film and video, and organized sport subdomains.
observations.uncertainty: Subdomain estimates are product-perspective economic-account indicators and are seasonally adjusted. The release notes revisions, price effects, event timing, and methodology boundaries; they do not identify audience behavior, platform concentration, worker transitions, or causal effects of major events.
observations.subgroup: Canadian culture subdomains: broadcasting, film and video, and organized sport.
observations.counterinterpretation: Broadcasting growth may reflect event rights, advertising, pricing, or accounting allocation rather than broad cultural demand; film/video job loss may reflect project timing rather than durable decline.

boundary: This record adds a national cultural-production and labor-market layer beneath consumer participation. It does not establish worker income, job quality, cultural access, audience demand, firm profitability, platform power, or causal effects of sporting events; the series remains revision-sensitive.
